pr_title: Use Boto waiters instead of customer _await_status method for RDS Operators
pr_body:
Closes: #27096
Related: #27076

### Summary

This PR replaces the status-check/waiter logic in `RdsBaseOperator` and `RdsBaseSensor` with `RdsHook` methods that use boto waiters where possible. All changes are backward compatible.

Please see "Files changed" for detailed information about updates and technical decisions/tradeoffs.

### Todo

- [x] Code changes
- [x] Unit test updates/additions

issue_context.title: Use Boto waiters instead of customer _await_status method for RDS Operators
issue_context.body:
### Description

Currently some code in RDS Operators use boto waiters and some uses a custom `_await_status`, the former is preferred over the later (waiters are vetted code provided by the boto sdk, they have features like exponential backoff, etc). See [this discussion thread](https://github.com/apache/airflow/pull/27076#discussion_r997325535) for more details/context.

### Use case/motivation

_No response_

_No response_

### Are you willing to submit a PR?

comments: I will work on this issue. Please assign me.

review_comments: When boto waiters aren't available, I pass a closure like this to a generic waiter method so that we can reuse waiting logic.

For each of the following resources, I added:
1. A method to get the resource state
2. A method to wait for the resource to reach a certain state

Resources:
- db instance
- db cluster
- db snapshot
- db cluster snapshot
- export task
- event subscription

In the current implementation, `RdsBaseOperator` and `RdsBaseSensor` each have a method that calls the appropriate boto "describe" function based on a string (like "db_snapshot" or "event_subscription").

https://github.com/apache/airflow/blob/64174ce25ae800a38e712aa0bd62a5893ea2ff99/airflow/providers/amazon/aws/operators/rds.py#L49-L66

I considered just moving this logic over to `RdsHook`, but decided to split it up because the existence (and variety) of boto waiters depends on the resource. For example, the db snapshot resource has 3 boto waiters, the db cluster snapshot resource has 2, and the export task resource has none.

One could maybe reduce the amount of code by keep a separate list of resources and their waiters and dynamically choosing at runtime, but I didn't go that far.
The default boto waiter delay seems to be 30 for all waiters, but `max_attempts` varies from 40~60. I (arbitrarily) opted to go with 40 everywhere.

From the name, this test is supposed to check the "no wait" condition, but `wait_for_completion` was set to `True`. This wasn't caught [for the above reason](https://github.com/apache/airflow/pull/27410/files#r1009685212).
`mock_await_status` wasn't being used (but was probably intended to be) so I added it.
You do not need to specify `wait_statuses` when using `RdsHook` waiter methods.
Basically the same updates as `operators/rds.py`
Fix: `DB_CLUSTER_SNAPSHOT` → `DB_INSTANCE_SNAPSHOT`
The methods tested here are gone now
Replaced the mocked "wait" method in all RDS operator unit tests.
The logic tested here is gone now
`db_type` is a template field, but we were casting it to `RdsDbType` in the constructor, which will raise an exception if we pass a template expression.

I see `no overload exists for ...` mypy warnings here because I'm creating the waiter name dynamically. The `if` statement one line above assures we aren't creating a waiter that doesn't exist so I ignore the warning. If someone has a more appropriate solution, please let me know.
Replaced with individual `RdsHook` methods.
Added test cases for each method in `RdsHook`
Making sure that boto waiters are used when available
Making sure custom waiter logic calls the generic waiter method, and the correct boto resource "describe" method
This sensor checks the existence of a snapshot associated with a db instance, but the unit tests didn't create the db instance.
Replaced calls to `_await_status` with `RdsHook` methods throughout this file.
This is a feature addition. A boto waiter for `db_snapshot_deleted` exists but wasn't used.
Nice! Love that! Could you add unit tests associated to this new feature?

`not_called` is not a method. `mock_await_status` is a mock, so the call does not raise an error, but it does not check the intended condition. Replaced with [`assert_not_called`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/unittest.mock.html#unittest.mock.Mock.assert_not_called) here and below.
